data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Arielle comes from the Hebrew word ‘ariel’ which means ‘lion of God’. The name is derived from the Bible where the word ‘ari-el’ is used to refer to God in His role as a fierce protector of His people. The name Arielle carries the meaning “Lioness of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Arielle usually hope their child will grow to embody lioness of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of strength and bravery for a young girl, inspiring her to face life's challenges with courage and faith.

in_hebrew.name: אריאל
in_hebrew.meaning: אריאל הוא שם שפירושו אריה של אלוהים או אלוהים הוא אריה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אריאל הוא שם עברי שמורכב משתי מילים: אריה ואל. אריה הוא סמל של כוח ואומץ, ואל הוא השם האלוהי. השם אריאל מופיע בתנ"ך (ישעיהו כה 2, יחזקאל ד 1) ככינוי לבית המקדש או לעיר ירושלים. השם אריאל משמש גם ככינוי לאריה שמייצג את אלוהים.

in_greek.name: Αριέλ
in_greek.meaning: Αριέλ σημαίνει λιοντάρι του Θεού ή ο Θεός είναι λιοντάρι
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αριέλ προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει λιοντάρι του Θεού ή ο Θεός είναι λιοντάρι. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Αριέλ, αλλά η ετυμολογία του συνδέεται με τη βιβλική παράδοση. Το όνομα Αριέλ έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί στην Εκκλησία από τους πρώτους χρόνους ως σύμβολο του θάρρους και της δύναμης που προέρχεται από τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Arielle
in_latin.meaning: Arielle significat leonem Dei vel Deus est leo
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Arielle originem habet in lingua hebraica et significat leonem Dei vel Deus est leo. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Arielle non invenitur directe in Scripturis, sed etymologia eius connectitur cum traditione biblica. Nomen Arielle usitatum est in Ecclesia a primis temporibus ut symbolum fortitudinis et audaciae quae a Deo procedit.

in_english.name: Arielle
in_english.meaning: Arielle means lioness of God or God is my lion
in_english.long_meaning: The name Arielle originates from Hebrew, meaning 'lioness of God' or 'God is my lion.' It is derived from two Hebrew words: 'ari,' meaning lion, and 'el,' meaning God. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, its etymology connects to biblical tradition. Historically, the name has been used in Christian contexts to symbolize courage and strength derived from God. It signifies a person of strong faith, courageous, and determined.

data.cultural_impact: The name Arielle has been popularized in various spheres of culture, most notably in literature and music. The most famous representation of the name is in the novel "The Lady of the Lake" by French author Francois-Madeleine de Montpensier, where the heroine's name is Ariadne, later anglicized as Arielle. This romantic tale tells the story of a young maiden who falls in love with a knight, and the name has been used as a symbol of feminine beauty, grace, and charm ever since. In music, French singer Arielle Dombasle has made the name famous with her soulful voice and eclectic mix of musical genres.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Arielle lies in its connection to the divine. As a name derived from the Hebrew word for 'lion of God', it serves as a constant reminder of the power and protection bestowed upon those who bear it. It suggests a deep, unyielding faith in God and a belief in His presence and intervention in one's life. The name Arielle also carries with it a sense of strength, courage, and valor, reflecting the fierce and unwavering nature of the Lord. It is a name that calls forth a deeply spiritual connection to the divine, and a reminder of the strength and comfort that comes from God's universal love and protection.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Arielle, meaning "lioness of God," embodies the strength and courage of a fierce yet gentle guardian. Her name symbolizes the divine feminine, connecting her to the power and wisdom of the divine feminine mysteries.

biblical_reference.note: Arielle is related to Ariel, a term used in Isaiah 29:1-2 to refer to Jerusalem or the altar.

historical_references.reference: Ariadne, a Cretan princess from Greek mythology, was the wife of Theseus and the goddess of the maze. Arielle is believed to be named after her, and is thought to have originated from the French interpretation of her name as 'most holy' or 'most beautiful'.

In medieval literature, a character named Arielle appears in several works, including the French romance 'Ariadne', written in the 13th century. She is depicted as a fairy or nymph who helps the hero recover his lost love.
